title: Do the two big rhesus monkey caloric-restriction studies actually disagree?
question: The Wisconsin (UW) and National Institute on Aging (NIA) rhesus monkey studies reached different conclusions about caloric restriction and survival. Using the joint reanalysis, report what each study found, which design differences could explain the conflict, and what this does and does not establish for humans.
verdict_question: Do the NIA and UW studies agree on whether caloric restriction extends monkey survival?

source.title: Caloric restriction improves health and survival of rhesus monkeys
source.license: CC BY 4.0; verify before reusing text

fields: key design differences that could explain the conflict
whether lifespan extension in humans is established
acceptance_criteria: Report each study's survival result separately, with its statistic or source location
Explain how control animals were fed at each site
Cover diet composition and age of onset as candidate explanations
Note that longevity was not a primary outcome at either site
Do not treat monkey survival as evidence of human lifespan extension
